title: Multimode experiment scheduler and rollback simulator for safe AB/shadow launches
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: We need a repeatable, auditable way to schedule and execute experiments (A/B tests, gradual canaries, and shadow runs) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments while validating config parity and environment constraints before exposing production traffic. Current rollout tooling covers traffic splitting and simple canaries but lacks: (1) a deterministic rollback simulator that exercises fallbacks under heterogenous infra; (2) per-tenant safelist/denylist lanes for private deployments with restricted features; (3) an experiment scheduler that sequences warm-up (KV/cache), synthetic traffic, latency/accuracy measurement windows, and auto-rollback triggers consistently across modes.

Goal: Build an "Experiment Scheduler" + "Rollback Simulator" that: (a) compiles a multimode experiment plan from a single declarative manifest; (b) validates required capabilities per environment (e.g., KMS availability, kernel/quantization compat, burst capacity on Dedicated); (c) orchestrates warm-up lanes and synthetic traffic injection; (d) simulates failure and overload scenarios to validate rollback policies; (e) exposes a dry-run report and an auditable runbook for SRE/SE review; (f) integrates with Console dashboards and Optimize recommendations to auto-suggest safe batch sizes/quant profiles for the experiment workload.

Acceptance criteria:
- Single YAML/JSON manifest can express: mode routing (hosted/dedicated/private), percent splits, experiment variants, warm-up steps, synthetic traffic profiles, roll-forward and rollback criteria.
- Preflight validator runs and returns a human-readable checklist of environment gaps and a machine-readable compatibility score.
- Rollback simulator can replay the manifest with injected faults (node loss, increased latency, cache cold-start) and produce a timeline showing when auto-rollback would trigger.
- Scheduler enforces safelists for Private tenants and refuses to run experiments that require unavailable features (e.g., hardware quantization not supported in on-prem package) unless forced with an explicit high-risk consent tag.
- End-to-end test harness (integration) runs experiments against a synthetic cluster and a staging Dedicated allocation; results are visible in Console.

Non-goals: full rework of existing traffic router or changing existing traffic splitting APIs. This feature composes with existing controller and admission layers.
comments: 2026-02-16: Discovery w/ PM and SRE. Decision: single-declarative-manifest is preferred for cross-mode parity. PM (Liang Chen) emphasized audit trail + human readable preflight report.

2026-02-18: Spike results: implemented minimal preflight validator. Found mismatch: Private on-prem packages lack our local KMS shim; created compatibility rule set (KMS, HSM, quant kernel availability, burst-capacity).

2026-02-22: Design review with Runtime/Console teams. Agreed to implement simulator as offline dry-run that reuses admission-controller predicates. Console will consume simulator result via artifacts link.

2026-02-25: Security review kickoff. Noted requirement for tenant-scoped safelist and explicit consent text when forcing experiments that bypass compatibility checks. Security requested logging at token-level for experiment orchestration steps.

2026-02-28: Prototype: scheduler can sequence (1) kv-cache-warmup lane, (2) micro-burst synthetic traffic, (3) measurement window. Initial simulator run shows auto-rollback triggers under 3x latency multiplier in Dedicated staging cluster.

2026-03-01: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4267 (scheduler + simulator core). Needs runtime tests and Console integration. Noted failing unit: stable time-window alignment across nodes (clock skew handling).

2026-03-02: Action items: (A) add NTP/clock-check step to preflight; (B) add explicit private-tenant consent flow in Console; (C) wire simulator artifacts to /console/experiments/{id}/report. Assigned tasks to SRE for synthetic traffic harness guidance (SRE-issues linked in Drive).
